appendix.title: Relation to BSF4ooRexx and .JSObject
appendix.para: The design follows Rony G. Flatscher's BSF4ooRexx, moved from Java to Python. PyObject is to Python objects what BSF.CLS's proxies are to Java objects, and oorexx.RexxObject what RexxProxy is to Rexx objects in Java, with the same sendMessage methods. box takes BSF4ooRexx's argument order, the routines are named as bsf.import and bsf.redirectTo, and the standard streams take bsf.redirectTo's arguments and its prefixes. PyArrayProxy is BSF_Array_Reference's counterpart.

Its sister in the ooRexx/WASM project, .JSObject, shares the shape: proxies by reference, names in any case with an exact form, and Rexx classes that extend classes of the other side (.py~extend, .js~extend, as ooRexx/.NET's .net~extend).
Python departs from both where Python itself differs: it never turns a string into a number, so the bridge converts numbers (), and o[k] is its own indexing, from 0.
